raw_response:
I’m 62 this year, and I’ve worked this land all my life, so I don’t chase fancy things. With only 10.1 mu and just myself in the house, I have to keep the plan steady and manageable. Cotton is still my main crop because I know it best, and around here if I manage water and topdressing well, it still gives me a stable return. But I won’t put everything into cotton. Chili brings cash if the market is decent, though it needs more labor and more pesticide watching, so I only keep a small area. Mungbean is simpler, cheaper, and safer on the wallet, so I use some land for that to spread risk. I’ve got well water, but pumping costs money, so I irrigate at the important stages, not too many times. Fertilizer-wise, I mostly follow what has worked on my fields: base fertilizer first, then one or two topdressings depending on how the crop looks. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go weak, but with only one worker at home I also can’t make the management too fine.
